Something with list selection I think.

Did some code review, still have to check 2D editor and the new manipulator.

Tested locally on several 2D demos, it works as expected. Code looks good to me.

Some feedback:

- This really encourages you to use grouping/locking to make runtime manipulation more viable. Example with getting coins in the 2D platformer without having to move around 🙂 
  - Notice how the two coins at the end move faster, because I forgot to lock their parent node, which causes double translation (both parent + children getting moved at the same time).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b2c22b3-7d9a-4f05-88da-9621826ffed1

- When Pan mode is disabled and you drag the scene while holding <kbd>Space</kbd>, it will pan but also move what's underneath the mouse cursor:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7daac34e-54c9-4e3a-a254-3535d51ec1fc

This does not occur in the editor, where it works as expected.

- This isn't specific to this PR, but if the *first* node you selected is freed while you're manipulating it, you lose the selection of all nodes. Ideally, it should reselect with the second node onwards to avoid losing the whole selection.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f571525e-8842-46ee-91c9-10c742d10b22

Happens when 3D camera manipulation is enabled.
Also the previous crash happens when you try to move a node inside a container. Both in editor and at runtime.

I also reviewed the CanvasItemEditor changes. I see lots of functionality moved to CanvasItemManipulator, that isn't used at runtime. E.g. grid, ruler and guides. I assume this is for some technical reason?

From other bugs, the temp pivot (Shift+drag in pivot tool) can't be set in the editor, only at runtime. Also it doesn't reset when selection changes.
Tested again on several demos, everything seems to work as expected. Great work :slightly_smiling_face:

I'm approving this because the changes are conceptually good usability-wise, even though I can't get all functionality to work on my Mac for weird QA reasons... which I suspect will float to the surface once more people start trying them out?
